nodes.name: Notation for number sets
nodes.statement: In the present paper, we employ the following notations: \[{\bf N}:=\{1,2,...\},~~{\bf N}_{0}:={\bf N}\cup\{0\},~~{\bf Z}_{0}^{-}:={\bf Z}^{-}\cup\{0\},\] where the symbols ${\bf N}$ and ${\bf Z}$ denote the set of integer and natural numbers; as usual, the symbols ${\bf R}$ and ${\bf C}$ denote the set of real and complex numbers, respectively.

nodes.name: H_B and H_C generalize Appell's F_1 and F_2
nodes.statement: It is known that $H_{C}$ and $H_{B}$ are generalizations of Appell's hypergeometric functions $F_{1}$ and $F_{2}$, while $H_{A}$ is the generalization of both $F_{1}$ and $F_{2}$.
conclusions: $H_{C}$ and $H_{B}$ are generalizations of Appell's hypergeometric functions $F_{1}$ and $F_{2}$, while $H_{A}$ is the generalization of both $F_{1}$ and $F_{2}$

nodes.name: Srivastava's triple hypergeometric function $H_B$
nodes.statement: In the present study, we confine our attention to Srivastava's triple hypergeometric function $H_{B}$ given by \cite[p. 43, 1.5(11) to 1.5(13)]{AB37} (see also \cite{AB34} and \cite[p.~68]{AB36}) \[ H_{B}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z) :=\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(b_{1})_{m+k}(b_{2})_{m+n}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}} \frac{x^{m}}{m!}\frac{y^{n}}{n!}\frac{z^{k}}{k!}\] \begin{equation} =\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(b_{1}\!+\!b_2)_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}}\,\frac{B(b_1\!+\!m\!+\!k,b_2\!+\!m\!+\!n)}{B(b_1,b_2)}\, \frac{x^{m}}{m!}\frac{y^{n}}{n!}\frac{z^{k}}{k!}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Srivastava's $H_B$ as a triple series in Pochhammer symbols, rewritten with a Beta-function ratio.

nodes.name: Pochhammer symbol and classical Beta function
nodes.statement: Here $(\lambda)_{n}$ denotes the Pochhammer symbol (or the shifted factorial, since $(1)_{n}=n!)$ defined by \[ (\lambda)_n:=\frac{\Gamma(\lambda+n)}{\Gamma(\lambda)}=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}1, & (n=0,\ \lambda\in{\bf C}\backslash\{0\})\\ \lambda(\lambda+1)...(\lambda+n-1), & (n\in{\bf N},~\lambda\in{\bf C}) \end{array}\right. \] and $B(\alpha, \beta)$ denotes the classical Beta function defined by \cite[(5.12.1)]{AB26} \begin{equation} B(\alpha, \beta)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll} \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{1}t^{\alpha-1}(1-t)^{\beta-1}dt}, & (\Re(\alpha)>0, \Re(\beta)>0)\\ \\ \displaystyle{\frac{\Gamma(\alpha)\Gamma(\beta)}{\Gamma(\alpha+\beta)}}, & ( (\alpha,\beta)\in{\bf C}\backslash {\bf Z}_{0}^{-}). \end{array}\right. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Defines the Pochhammer symbol $(\lambda)_n=\Gamma(\lambda+n)/\Gamma(\lambda)$ and the Beta function $B(\alpha,\beta)$.

nodes.name: Classical Beta function
nodes.statement: B(\alpha, \beta)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll} \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{1}t^{\alpha-1}(1-t)^{\beta-1}dt}, & (\Re(\alpha)>0, \Re(\beta)>0)\\ \\ \displaystyle{\frac{\Gamma(\alpha)\Gamma(\beta)}{\Gamma(\alpha+\beta)}}, & ( (\alpha,\beta)\in{\bf C}\backslash {\bf Z}_{0}^{-}). \end{array}\right.
nodes.label: ES5

nodes.name: Convergence region of $H_B$
nodes.statement: The convergence region for Srivastava's triple hypergeometric series $H_{B}(\cdot)$ is given in \cite[ p.243]{ab22} as $|x|<\alpha$, $|y|<\beta$, $|z|<\gamma$, where $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ satisfy the relation $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+2\sqrt{\alpha\beta\gamma}=1$.

nodes.name: Exton's triple hypergeometric function $X_4$
nodes.statement: A different type of triple hypergeometric function is Exton's function $ X_{4}(\cdot)$, which is defined by (see \cite{AB19} and \cite[p.~84, Entry (45a)]{AB37}) \begin{equation} X_{4}(b_{1},b_{2};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z):=\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(b_{1})_{2m+n+k}(b_{2})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}} \frac{x^{m}}{m!}\frac{y^{n}}{n!}\frac{z^{k}}{k!}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Convergence region of $X_4$
nodes.statement: The convergence region for this series is $2\sqrt{|x|}+(\sqrt{|y|}+\sqrt{|z|})^{2}<1$.

nodes.name: $H_B^{(a)}$ with additional parameter $a$
nodes.statement: We shall also find it convenient to introduce an additional parameter $a$ into $H_B(\cdot)$ in the form \[H_{B}^{(a)}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z):=\hspace{6cm}\] \begin{equation} \sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(b_{1}\!+\!b_2)_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}}\,\frac{B(b_1\!+\!a\!+\!m\!+\!k,b_2\!+\!a\!+\!m\!+\!n)}{B(b_1,b_2)}\, \frac{x^{m}}{m!}\frac{y^{n}}{n!}\frac{z^{k}}{k!}, \end{equation} which reduces to (\ref{PV2}) when $a=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Variant $H_B^{(a)}$ of $H_B$ with both Beta arguments shifted by $a$.

nodes.name: Extended Beta function $B(x,y;p)$
nodes.statement: In 1997, Chaudhry {\it et al.} \cite[Eq.(1.7)]{AB8} gave a $p$-extension of the Beta function $B(x, y)$ given by \[B(x,y; p)= \int_0^1 t^{x-1}(1-t)^{y-1}\,\exp \left[\frac{-p}{t(1-t)}\right]dt,\qquad (\Re (p)>0)\] and they proved that this extension has connections with the Macdonald, error and Whittaker functions.

nodes.name: Definition of $B_{p,\nu}$
nodes.statement: B_{p,\nu}(x,y)=\sqrt{\frac{2p}{\pi}}\displaystyle{\int_{0}^{1}t^{x-\frac{3}{2}}(1-t)^{y-\frac{3}{2}}} K_{\nu+\frac{1}{2}}\left(\frac{p}{t(1-t)}\right)dt,

nodes.name: Convergence region of $H_{B,p,\nu}$
nodes.statement: The region of convergence is $|x|<r$, $|y|<s$, $|z|<t$, where $r+s+t+2\sqrt{rst}=1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: \textbf{Proof}:\ The proof of the first integral representation (\ref{PV17}) follows by use of the extended beta function (\ref{ES20}) in (\ref{PV16}), a change the order of integration and summation (with uniform convergence of the integral) and, after simplification, use of Exton's triple hypergeometric function (\ref{PV3}), to obtain the right-hand side of the result (\ref{PV17}). The integral representations (\ref{PV18})-(\ref{PV23}) can be proved directly by using the following transformations \begin{eqnarray*} (\ref{PV18}):\qquad t&=&\frac{(\beta-\gamma)(\xi-\alpha)}{(\beta-\alpha)(\xi-\gamma)},\quad \frac{dt}{d\xi}=\frac{(\beta-\gamma)(\alpha-\gamma)}{(\beta-\alpha) (\xi-\gamma)^2},\\ (\ref{PV20}):\qquad t&=& \sin^2 \xi,\quad \frac{dt}{d\xi}=2\sin \xi \cos \xi\\ (\ref{PV21}):\qquad t&=&\frac{(1+\lambda)\sin^{2}\xi}{1+\lambda \sin^{2}\xi},\quad\frac{dt}{d\xi}=\frac{2(1+\lambda)\sin \xi \cos \xi}{(1+\lambda \sin^2 \xi)^2},\\ (\ref{PV23}):\qquad t&=&\frac{\lambda \sin^{2}\xi}{\cos^2{\xi}+\lambda \sin^{2}\xi},\quad \frac{dt}{d\xi}=\frac{2\lambda \sin \xi \cos \xi}{(\cos^2\xi+\lambda \sin^2\xi)^2}\\ \end{eqnarray*} in turn in (\ref{PV17}) to obtain the right-hand side of each result.
nodes.statement_short: Insert the integral for $B_{p,\nu}$ into the series, swap sum and integral, identify $X_4$; the rest by changes of variable.

nodes.name: Mellin transform
nodes.statement: The Mellin transform of a locally integrable function $f(x)$ on $(0,\infty)$ is given by (see, for example, \cite[p.193, Section 2.1]{AB125}) \begin{equation} \Phi(s)={\cal M}\left\{f(x)\right\}(s)=\int_{0}^{\infty}x^{s-1}f(x)\,dx \end{equation} which defines an analytic function in its strip of analyticity $a<\Re (s)<b$.

nodes.name: Mellin transform
nodes.statement: \Phi(s)={\cal M}\left\{f(x)\right\}(s)=\int_{0}^{\infty}x^{s-1}f(x)\,dx
nodes.label: PV27

nodes.name: Inverse Mellin transform
nodes.statement: The inverse Mellin transform of the above function (\ref{PV27}) is defined by \begin{equation} f(x)={\cal M}^{-1}\left\{\Phi(s)\right\}=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{c-i\infty}^{c+i\infty}x^{-s}\Phi(s)\,ds \qquad (a<c<b). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Inverse Mellin transform
nodes.statement: f(x)={\cal M}^{-1}\left\{\Phi(s)\right\}=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{c-i\infty}^{c+i\infty}x^{-s}\Phi(s)\,ds \qquad (a<c<b).

nodes.statement: Using the extended Beta function (\ref{ES20}) then shows that \[{\cal M}\left\{H_{B,p,\nu}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)\right\}(s) =\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(b_{1}+b_{2})_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}~B(b_{1},b_{2})}\frac{x^{m}}{m!}\frac{y^{n}}{n!}\frac{z^{k}}{k!}\] \[\times\int_{0}^{1}t^{b_{1}+m+k-\frac{3}{2}}(1-t)^{b_{2}+m+n-\frac{3}{2}} \left\{\int_{0}^{\infty}p^{s-\frac{1}{2}}K_{\nu+\frac{1}{2}}\left(\frac{p}{t(1-t)}\right)dp\right\}dt.\]
nodes.statement_short: Write $B_{p,\nu}$ as its Bessel-kernel integral.

nodes.name: Identify $H_B^{(s)}$
nodes.statement: Identifying the above sum as $H_B^{(s)}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)$ in (\ref{PV2a}), we obtain the right-hand side of (\ref{PV30}).
nodes.statement_short: Recognise the sum as $H_B^{(s)}$.

nodes.name: Differentiate termwise in $x$
nodes.statement: If we differentiate partially the series for ${\cal H}\equiv H_{B,p,\nu}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)$ in (\ref{PV16}) with respect to $x$ we obtain \[\frac{\partial{\cal H}}{\partial x} =\sum_{m=1}^\infty \sum_{n,k=0}^\infty \frac{(b_1+b_2)_{2m+n+k} (b_3)_{n+k}}{(c_1)_m(c_2)_n(c_3)_k}\,\frac{B_{p,\nu}(b_1+m+k,b_2+m+n)}{B(b_1, b_2)}\,\frac{x^{m-1}}{(m-1)!}\frac{y^n}{n!} \frac{z^k}{k!}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the defining series termwise in $x$.

nodes.name: Shift index and apply Beta identity
nodes.statement: Making use of the fact that \begin{equation} B(b_1,b_2)=\frac{(b_1+b_2)_2}{b_1 b_2}\,B(b_1+1, b_2+1) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Shift $m$ and use the Beta and Pochhammer identities to get (e41).

nodes.name: Iterate in $x$
nodes.statement: Repeated application of (\ref{e41}) then yields for $M=1, 2, \ldots $ \[\frac{\partial^M}{\partial x^M}{\cal H}= \frac{(b_1)_M (b_2)_M}{(c_1)_M}\,H_{B,p,\nu}(b_{1}+M,b_{2}+M,b_{3};c_{1}+M,c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z).\]
nodes.statement_short: Iterate (e41) $M$ times.

nodes.name: Differentiate once in $y$
nodes.statement: A similar reasoning shows that \[\frac{\partial^{M+1}}{\partial x^M \partial y}{\cal H} =\frac{(b_1)_M (b_2)_M}{(c_1)_M} \sum_{m,k=0}^\infty \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(b_1\!+\!b_2\!+\!2M)_{2m+n+k} (b_3)_{n+k}}{(c_1\!+\!M)_m (c_2)_n(c_3)_k}\hspace{3cm}\] \[\hspace{3cm}\times\frac{B_{p, \nu}(b_1\!+\!M\!+\!m\!+\!k,b_2\!+\!M\!+\!n\!+\!k)}{B(b_1\!+\!M, b_2\!+\!M)}\,\frac{x^m}{m!} \frac{y^{n-1}}{(n-1)!}\frac{z^k}{k!}\] \begin{equation} =\frac{(b_1)_{M} (b_2)_{M+1} b_3}{(c_1)_{M}c_2}\,H_{B,p,\nu}(b_1+M,b_2+M+1,b_3+1;c_1+M,c_2+1,c_3;x,y,z) \end{equation} upon putting $n\to n+1$ and using the property of the Beta function in (\ref{ES5}).
nodes.statement_short: Same index-shift argument for one $y$-derivative gives (e42).

nodes.name: Iterate in $y$
nodes.statement: Repeated differentiation of (\ref{e42}) $N$ times with respect to $y$ then produces \[\frac{\partial^{M+N}}{\partial x^M \partial y^N} {\cal H}=\frac{(b_1)_M (b_2)_{M+N} (b_3)_N}{(c_1)_M (c_2)_N}\, H_{B,p,\nu}(b_1\!+\!M,b_2\!+\!M\!+\!N,b_3\!+\!N;c_1\!+\!M,c_2\!+\!N,c_3;x,y,z).\]
nodes.statement_short: Iterate (e42) $N$ times.

nodes.name: Iterate in $z$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Application of the same procedure to deal with differentiation with respect to $z$ then yields the result stated in (\ref{PV37}).
nodes.statement_short: The same for $z$ yields (PV37).

nodes.statement: For ease of presentation we shall assume that the parameters $b_j$, $c_j>0$ ($1\leq j\leq 3$).

nodes.statement_short: Decompose the series into three sums (e61).

nodes.name: Shift index in first sum
nodes.statement_short: Name the first extra sum $S$ and shift $n$.

nodes.name: Apply Beta identity
nodes.statement_short: Use $B(b_1,b_2)=\frac{b_1+b_2}{b_2}B(b_1,b_2+1)$ to identify (e62).

nodes.name: Second sum
nodes.statement: Proceeding in a similar manner for the second series in (\ref{e61}) with $k\to k+1$, we find that this sum can be expressed as \begin{equation} \frac{zb_1}{c_3} H_{B,p,\nu}(b_1+1,b_2,b_3+1;c_1, c_2,c_3+1; x,y,z). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Same argument for the second sum gives (e63).

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Combination of (\ref{e62}) and (\ref{e63}) with (\ref{e61}) then produces the result stated in (\ref{e60}).
nodes.statement_short: Combine the pieces into (e60).

nodes.name: Lower $c_1$ by one
nodes.statement: Consider the case when $c_1$ is reduced by 1, namely \[H\equiv H_{B,p,\nu}(b_1,b_2,b_3;c_1-1,c_2,c_3;x,y,z)\] and use $(c_1-1)_m=(c_1)_m/\{1+\frac{m}{c_1-1}\}$.

nodes.name: Expand
nodes.statement_short: Split off the extra sum weighted by $m/(c_1-1)$.

nodes.name: Shift index
nodes.statement_short: Shift $m$ in the extra sum.

nodes.name: Apply Beta identity
nodes.statement_short: Apply (eB) to identify a shifted $H_{B,p,\nu}$.
